rca_of_the_issue: Original bug: automations.github_webhook accepted requests when GITHUB_WEBHOOK_SECRET env var was unset (fail-open branch executed the push handler on any signature-less request). Reproduction: curl -X POST <base>/api/aurem-dev/automations/webhook/github with fake JSON body and no X-Hub-Signature-256 header returned 200 and processed the push. Fix: automations.py github_webhook() now short-circuits to HTTP 403 'Webhook not configured — signature verification unavailable' whenever GITHUB_WEBHOOK_SECRET is missing, and HTTP 401 on wrong/absent signature when the secret IS set. Verified via 3 layers: (1) live curl on preview -> 403 for both no-signature and bad-signature paths, (2) unit tests in test_master_task_2026_09_28_webhook_signature.py exercising all 5 branches (secret unset, missing sig, wrong sig, correct sig+push, correct sig+non-push), (3) related iter78 tests updated to expect 403. Parallel hardening: 57 legacy cto_automations rows paused with paused_reason='MASTER_TASK_2026_09_28_security_audit', and 3 feature flags (user_automations_page, user_analytics_page, public_ship_wall) gate the corresponding endpoints/routes/nav so even authenticated users cannot resurface the shipwall/analytics/automations attack surface until an explicit re-enable.
